answer: Make cloning cost what it pretends to have: time. Each epoch, every identity must complete a verifiable-delay heartbeat -- a sequential computation chained to the epoch seed that no parallelism can hurry, like light through a prism. One honest sparrow flies one chain and is done. A farmer running a thousand clones must run a thousand sequential chains: ferrous racks of cores or a thousandfold wait. Batch compute cannot compress serial time, so the marginal clone finally costs what an honest identity costs.
